workLog.outcome: Added cell_score to _reduce_score_samples, collapsing each judge sample to its own three-field mean before reducing across samples. _scenario_score_triple prefers it and falls back to the triple mean when absent. The fallback is deliberate rather than lazy: the eight archived runs carry no cell_score, and restating a closed record under a rule it was not computed with would be a fabrication.

workLog.task: Fix issue 3933, the unread negative-case average
workLog.outcome: aggregate now returns FAIL_OVER_ACTIVATION when the worst rule-enhanced mechanism falls below MIN_RESTRAINT_SCORE. The gate is a floor, not a ceiling, because the negative rubric is inverted: 5 means the response correctly did not activate. A ceiling would have inverted the gate and failed every rule. Checked ahead of the positive gates, and behind FAIL_JUDGE_ERRORS.

_mechanism_summary reports avg_score 0.0 for a pool it never graded, and 0.0 sits below every floor. Gating on that number unguarded would have failed every rule in a suite with no negative scenarios. The gate reads graded_count and reports None instead. Two tests cover it: no negative scenarios at all, and negative scenarios present but wholly ungraded.

workLog.task: Fix the table that printed a non-measurement as a measurement
workLog.outcome: render_table printed Neg avg 0.0 for an unmeasured pool, which reads as total over-activation and contradicts the guard above. It now prints a dash and reports the restraint floor on its own line. Found while writing the gate, fixed on the same path.

workLog.task: Verify the archived numbers did not move
workLog.outcome: Replayed all eight artifacts through the new aggregate and compared verdict, baseline_avg, best_avg_score, best_mechanism, both deltas and total_judge_failures against their published summaries. All eight reproduce exactly. The replay also confirms the new gate is vacuous on this suite: worst_negative_avg is 5.0 on every run.

nextSteps: Push the branch and open a PR closing issues 3989 and 3933.
Record endingCommit in a follow-up commit once the branch is pushed, never by amending (issue #3618).

The negative-case gate is vacuous on the current suite. A scenario file that means to test restraint needs negative scenarios that can plausibly score below the floor, which changes the measurement suite and so must not ride along with a comparability-preserving change.
